findings.title: Global byte-limit failure is swallowed, so copying and storage checks continue beyond the declared bound
findings.detail: The cumulative counter is incremented after a full file is received, then total_file_limit raises ValueError inside a per-file handler that catches it and continues. Subsequent files still receive their full per-file command limit. The 25MiB allowance caps persisted file content, not aggregate received content. Global exhaustion does not stop ordinary work or mark report.error.
findings.reproduction: Run the unchanged capture with synthetic metadata matching the pinned eleven subjects, fake native/HTTP runners and one allowed-size 1MiB regular file per selected path. It receives 97517568 bytes (93MiB), makes all93 file copies and then both storage exec checks; persists25 files and returns READY_FOR_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW with inventory_preserved=true.
findings.shortest_correction: Make aggregate exhaustion terminal for normal capture work, distinct from an ordinary missing/invalid file. Bound the next file transfer/validation by the remaining global allowance and do not issue further cp/storage/HTTP work once exhausted. Retain the reserved final inventory and sanitized INCOMPLETE partial report. Add a whole-capture fake-runner regression; no framework changes or native retry is needed.
